# laravel_cloud_database_snapshot (Resource)

Manages a snapshot of a Laravel Cloud database cluster.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "laravel_cloud_database_cluster" "example" {
  name   = "my-db"
  type   = "laravel_mysql_84"
  region = "us-east-2"

  # `config` is an opaque JSON document whose shape depends on the database
  # type. Every key the API returns must be present, with exactly the value it
  # stores, or the next plan shows a permanent diff. Discover the schema and
  # the valid `size` enum with `GET /databases/types`.
  config = jsonencode({
    size                     = "mysql-flex-512mb"
    storage                  = 10
    is_public                = false
    uses_scheduled_snapshots = false
    retention_days           = 7
    suspend_seconds          = 0
  })
}

resource "laravel_cloud_database_snapshot" "example" {
  cluster_id = laravel_cloud_database_cluster.example.id
  name       = "nightly"
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `cluster_id` (String) Database cluster ID.
- `name` (String) Snapshot name (1-100 characters).

### Optional

- `description` (String) Snapshot description (3-40 characters).

### Read-Only

- `completed_at` (String) Completion timestamp.
- `created_at` (String)
- `id` (String) The ID of this resource.
- `pitr_enabled` (Boolean) Whether point-in-time recovery is enabled for this snapshot.
- `pitr_ends_at` (String) Timestamp when point-in-time recovery coverage ends.
- `status` (String) Snapshot status.
- `storage_bytes` (Number) Storage size in bytes.
- `type` (String) Snapshot type.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
terraform import laravel_cloud_database_snapshot.example "{snapshot_id}"
```
